introduction.title: Memory
introduction.explanation: The robot can only remember a few things, and each slot holds one kind: a number, a yes or no, a direction or a place. Places count from 0, like real code: the top left tile is column 0, row 0.

realWords.text: A memory slot is a variable: a named place that holds a value. The word let makes a new one. Then come its name, its type, and the value it starts with.
The word after the colon is the variable's type: the kind of value it may hold. number means numbers only. TypeScript checks types before the program runs, so the wrong kind is caught early.
A yes or no value is called a boolean. In code, yes is written true and no is written false. Every condition in an if or a while is a boolean.
One equals sign does not ask a question. It takes the value on its right and puts it in the variable on its left. That is called assigning, and the value that was there before is gone.
